section_summary: This section covers proposed changes to Japanese fishing limits, Korean opposition to a rumored extension of the MacArthur Line, and plans for Japanese fishery inspections. A long despatch and memorandum examine Soviet and Japanese claims to the Kuril Islands, the Habomai Islands, and Shikotan, arguing that their history and fishing value should inform a peace settlement. The section also includes a brief report on preparations for a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.

subfiles.title: Discrepancy between proposed Japanese fishing area and SCAPIN 1033/1
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests that the Department alert the Far Eastern Commission to an omitted productive fishing area.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo reports a discrepancy between proposed fishing limits and SCAPIN 1033/1 and requests corrective action.

subfiles.title: Amendment to proposed Japanese fishing area
subfiles.to: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports an amendment aligning proposed fishing limits with SCAPIN 1033/1.
subfiles.summary: An amendment has been introduced in the Far Eastern Commission Steering Committee to correct the boundary.

subfiles.title: Korean Reaction to Rumored Extension of Japanese Fishing Limits
subfiles.about: Reports Korean official and press opposition to a rumored extension of the MacArthur Line.
subfiles.summary: Korean officials and newspapers feared an extension toward Korean waters. SCAP representatives said no such extension was planned and described any future change as southward and eastward.

subfiles.title: Press interview with Foreign Minister Ben Limb
subfiles.from: United States Information Service, American Embassy, Seoul
subfiles.about: Records Ben Limb's objections to expanding Japanese fishing limits and his answers on other foreign-policy questions.
subfiles.summary: Limb presents six Korean objections to extending the MacArthur Line, then discusses U.S. troop withdrawal, Chinese communists, and displaced persons.

subfiles.title: The Whole Nation Protests Against the Extension of MacArthur Line
subfiles.about: Opposes Japanese access to fishing grounds near Korea.
subfiles.summary: The editorial portrays extension as a threat to Korean fisheries, security, and Asian confidence in the United States.

subfiles.title: The Change of the US Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Criticizes U.S. policy toward Japan and the proposed fishing-line extension.
subfiles.summary: The editorial urges U.S. officials to consider Korean interests when setting Japanese fishing limits.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation on extension of the MacArthur Line
subfiles.about: Records SCAP assurances about the direction and timing of any fishing-limit extension.
subfiles.summary: Richard Finn says SCAP has no plan to extend limits toward Korea and wants Japanese compliance before any expansion.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Korean Foreign Ministry officials about the MacArthur Line
subfiles.about: Records Korean officials' request for assurances that Japanese fishing limits would not move toward Korea.
subfiles.summary: Macdonald relays SCAP's assurances to Hong and Kim; the ministry subsequently seeks a written response.

subfiles.title: Request for written information on the MacArthur fishery line
subfiles.from: Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests written information about alteration of the MacArthur fishery line.
subfiles.summary: The ministry requests written information on the line.

subfiles.title: Embassy reply concerning the MacArthur Line
subfiles.to: Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Directs the ministry to its mission in Japan for SCAP's position on Japanese fishing limits.
subfiles.summary: The embassy advises the ministry to consult its mission chief's report of discussions with SCAP.

subfiles.title: Korean objection to proposed extension of the MacArthur Line
subfiles.about: Relays a Korean appeal against extending Japanese fishery rights into Korean waters.
subfiles.summary: The transmitted statement calls an extension economically and politically harmful to Korea and urges U.S. officials to reject it.

subfiles.title: Kuril Islands, the Habomai Islands, and Shikotan Island
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum on Soviet and Japanese island claims and recommends territorial reconsideration.
subfiles.summary: Huston argues that the Yalta agreement did not expressly cover the Habomai Islands and Shikotan, while later SCAP measures strengthened the apparent Soviet position. He cites Japanese history, fisheries, navigation, and strategic concerns in favor of restoring Etorofu, Kunashiri, Habomai, and Shikotan to Japan.

subfiles.title: Soviet and Japanese Territorial Claims to the Kuril Islands, the Habomai Islands, and Shikotan Island
subfiles.about: Examines competing island claims through wartime occupation, Allied directives, Japanese maps, treaties, and fisheries.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews Soviet seizures of Japanese fishing vessels and disputes whether Soviet occupation established sovereignty. It traces Yalta, SCAPIN 677, SCAPIN 1033, older Japanese maps, and the Shimoda and Saint Petersburg treaties. Spinks argues that Habomai and Shikotan were historically separate from the Kurils and recommends restoring them, Etorofu, and Kunashiri to Japan for historical, economic, navigational, and strategic reasons.

subfiles.title: Preparations for a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports disagreement over how to authorize preparations for the 1949–1950 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: GHQ sections differ over the directive needed to prepare vessels and finance the expedition.

subfiles.title: Directive Authorizing Japanese Fishery Inspection System
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposed SCAP directive and diplomatic notice concerning Japanese fishery inspections.
subfiles.summary: Huston describes an inspection plan using eleven vessels, defined operating limits, and an estimated appropriation of 150 million yen. He expects inspections to reduce violations and support a later fishing-area expansion.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fishery Inspection System
subfiles.doc_type: draft SCAP directive; enclosure 1 to despatch 424
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Authorizes a Japanese fishery inspection system with specified operating boundaries and restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The directive defines inspection duties, operating limits, vessel markings, voyage authorization, and the absence of police powers. It states that authorization does not determine sovereignty, boundaries, or fishing rights.

subfiles.title: Note for Record on the Japanese fishery inspection system
subfiles.doc_type: note for record appended to draft directive
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Explains fishing violations, the Japanese inspection proposal, its costs, and approval by the Chief of Staff.
subfiles.summary: The note cites 78 reported fishing-area violations, only three resulting convictions, and a Japanese proposal for eleven vessels, vessel identification and radio reporting, penalties, and equipment funding. It records Chief of Staff approval on June 24, 1949.
